pairs.reason: Both rely on markets and less bureaucracy rather than state control; they differ on the lever, opening markets to competition versus cutting taxes and spending.
Both act against the large companies that dominate markets, but one does it through competition and rejects government control while the other supervises prices and taxes profits.
Neither rules the other out, but one changes how markets work so prices fall over time and the other pays households and raises wages directly.
One shrinks the state and its taxes because people spend better than the state; the other has the state step in more, supervise prices and add a tax on profits.
Both aim to leave households with more money, but one cuts government spending and the other raises allowances and subsidies.
Both have the state act directly to ease prices; they differ on the target, supervising prices and companies versus allowances, wages and subsidies for households.
